title: Christmas Songs & Carols
tagline: Fa la la la… WRONG. Try again.
description: From candlelit carols to jukebox jingles: thirty questions on the songs everyone hums and nobody actually knows. Warm up those vocal cords.

questions.q: “Silent Night” was first written in which language?
questions.reveal: Ja! It’s “Stille Nacht”: words by Joseph Mohr, music by Franz Xaver Gruber, first sung in Oberndorf, Austria, on Christmas Eve 1818.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Silent Night — Joseph Mohr & Franz Xaver Gruber, 1818

questions.q: In “Jingle Bells,” how many horses are pulling that open sleigh?
questions.reveal: Just one, folks. James Lord Pierpont published it in 1857 as “The One Horse Open Sleigh.” Budget sleigh, maximum jingle.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Jingle Bells — James Lord Pierpont, 1857

questions.q: On the fifth day of Christmas, my true love gave to me… what?
questions.reveal: Five gold rings! The big, stretched-out “fiiive gold rings” comes from Frederic Austin’s 1909 arrangement. Belt it like you mean it.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: The Twelve Days of Christmas — traditional, arr. Frederic Austin, 1909

questions.q: Which name is NOT among the reindeer rattled off at the start of “Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer”?
questions.reveal: Blinky never made the team. The roll call: Dasher, Dancer, Prancer, Vixen, Comet, Cupid, Donner and Blitzen. Then, of course, Rudolph.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer — Johnny Marks, 1949

questions.q: “Deck the halls with boughs of…” what?
questions.reveal: Holly! Fa la la la la. The tune is the old Welsh New Year’s song “Nos Galan”; Thomas Oliphant’s English words date from 1862.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Deck the Hall — Welsh tune “Nos Galan”, English words Thomas Oliphant, 1862

questions.q: Who wrote and sang “Feliz Navidad,” the bilingual hit from 1970?
questions.reveal: José Feliciano! Spanish verse, English verse, and a chorus nobody can resist. Próspero año y felicidad, indeed.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Feliz Navidad — José Feliciano, 1970

questions.category: All I Want for Christmas Is You
questions.q: Who sings the 1994 smash “All I Want for Christmas Is You”?
questions.reveal: Mariah Carey, who co-wrote it with Walter Afanasieff. It finally hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in December 2019, 25 years later.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: All I Want for Christmas Is You — Mariah Carey & Walter Afanasieff, 1994

questions.q: Irving Berlin’s “White Christmas” debuted in the 1942 film Holiday Inn. Who sang it there?
questions.reveal: Bing Crosby! Guinness lists his recording as the best-selling single of all time. Not bad for a song about weather.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: White Christmas — Irving Berlin, 1942

questions.q: Finish the famous drum refrain of “The Little Drummer Boy”:
questions.reveal: Pa rum pum pum pum! Katherine K. Davis wrote it in 1941 as “Carol of the Drum.” The Harry Simeone Chorale made it a hit in 1958.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: The Little Drummer Boy — Katherine K. Davis, Henry Onorati & Harry Simeone, 1941

questions.category: Santa Claus Is Comin’ to Town
questions.q: Santa’s making a list and checking it… how often?
questions.reveal: Twice! J. Fred Coots and Haven Gillespie wrote it in 1934. Santa’s quality control is frankly better than most companies’.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Santa Claus Is Comin’ to Town — J. Fred Coots & Haven Gillespie, 1934

questions.q: Rudolph first appeared in a 1939 giveaway booklet from which retailer?
questions.reveal: Montgomery Ward! Robert L. May created Rudolph; his brother-in-law Johnny Marks wrote the song, and Gene Autry made it a hit in 1949.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer — Johnny Marks, 1949

questions.q: Which of these holiday standards never actually mentions Christmas?
questions.reveal: “Let It Snow!” is all about weather, a fire and a cozy evening. Sammy Cahn and Jule Styne wrote it in 1945. Christmas: zero mentions.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Let It Snow! Let It Snow! Let It Snow! — Sammy Cahn & Jule Styne, 1945

questions.category: Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas
questions.q: Judy Garland introduced “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas” in which 1944 film?
questions.reveal: Meet Me in St. Louis! Hugh Martin and Ralph Blane wrote it, and an early, gloomier draft of the lyric got brightened up before filming.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas — Hugh Martin & Ralph Blane, 1944

questions.q: How old was Brenda Lee when she recorded “Rockin’ Around the Christmas Tree” in 1958?
questions.reveal: Thirteen! And in December 2023 the song finally hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. Johnny Marks (yes, the Rudolph guy) wrote it.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Rockin’ Around the Christmas Tree — Johnny Marks, 1958

questions.q: “O Holy Night” began life in which language?
questions.reveal: French! Adolphe Adam set Placide Cappeau’s poem “Minuit, chrétiens” in 1847. John Sullivan Dwight wrote the familiar English version.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Minuit, chrétiens (O Holy Night) — Adolphe Adam & Placide Cappeau, 1847

questions.q: “O Come, All Ye Faithful” is a translation of which Latin hymn?
questions.reveal: Adeste Fideles! The Latin hymn is usually credited to John Francis Wade; Frederick Oakeley’s English translation came in 1841.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: O Come, All Ye Faithful — English trans. Frederick Oakeley, 1841

questions.q: Good King Wenceslas looked out on the Feast of… whom?
questions.reveal: Stephen! That’s December 26. John Mason Neale wrote the words in 1853. Fun twist: the real Wenceslas was a duke of Bohemia, only named king after his death.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Good King Wenceslas — John Mason Neale, 1853

questions.q: “What Child Is This?” is sung to which old English tune?
questions.reveal: Greensleeves! William Chatterton Dix wrote the words in 1865 and borrowed one of England’s most famous melodies.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: What Child Is This? — William Chatterton Dix, 1865

questions.q: Leroy Anderson’s “Sleigh Ride” ends with a trumpet imitating what?
questions.reveal: A horse whinny! Anderson finished the instrumental in 1948; Mitchell Parish added the lyrics in 1950. Giddy-yap, giddy-yap!

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Sleigh Ride — Leroy Anderson, 1948; lyrics Mitchell Parish, 1950

questions.q: In “Winter Wonderland,” who do the lovebirds pretend their snowman is?
questions.reveal: Parson Brown, a country preacher who could marry them. Felix Bernard and Richard B. Smith wrote it in 1934. Snowman ordination: unclear.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Winter Wonderland — Felix Bernard & Richard B. Smith, 1934

questions.category: Angels We Have Heard on High
questions.q: The long refrain “Gloria in excelsis Deo” is in which language?
questions.reveal: Latin, for “Glory to God in the highest.” The carol itself comes from the French “Les Anges dans nos campagnes.” Hold that Glooo-ria!

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Angels We Have Heard on High — French carol “Les Anges dans nos campagnes”

questions.category: I Heard the Bells on Christmas Day
questions.q: “I Heard the Bells on Christmas Day” comes from a Civil War-era poem by which American poet?
questions.reveal: Longfellow! He wrote “Christmas Bells” in 1863, in the middle of the Civil War. That’s why it wrestles with peace on earth.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Christmas Bells — Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, 1863

questions.q: “Carol of the Bells” began as the Ukrainian New Year’s song “Shchedryk.” What bird is its hero?
questions.reveal: A swallow, who promises a family a prosperous year. Mykola Leontovych arranged it; Peter J. Wilhousky wrote the English words in 1936.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Carol of the Bells — Mykola Leontovych; English lyrics Peter J. Wilhousky, 1936

questions.q: The tune of “Hark! The Herald Angels Sing” comes from a cantata by which composer?
questions.reveal: Mendelssohn (1840). Charles Wesley’s 1739 words originally opened “Hark how all the welkin rings.” Catchy? Not quite.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Hark! The Herald Angels Sing — Charles Wesley, 1739; music Felix Mendelssohn, 1840

questions.q: Handel’s Messiah, now a Christmas favorite, premiered in 1742 in which city?
questions.reveal: Dublin, on April 13, 1742. That’s right: it premiered in spring, just after Easter, not at Christmas. Hallelujah anyway!

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Messiah — George Frideric Handel, 1741

questions.q: Add up every gift in all twelve verses of “The Twelve Days of Christmas.” How many gifts in total?
questions.reveal: 364! Each day repeats all the earlier gifts, so it piles up fast. One for almost every day of the year. Hope your true love has storage.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: The Twelve Days of Christmas — traditional, arr. Frederic Austin, 1909

questions.q: Phillips Brooks wrote “O Little Town of Bethlehem” in 1868 while a rector in which US city?
questions.reveal: Philadelphia! Brooks had visited Bethlehem a few years earlier. His church organist, Lewis Redner, wrote the American tune.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: O Little Town of Bethlehem — Phillips Brooks & Lewis Redner, 1868

questions.q: Isaac Watts based the words of “Joy to the World” on which psalm?
questions.reveal: Psalm 98, “Make a joyful noise unto the Lord.” Watts published it in 1719. Joyful noise: achieved.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Joy to the World — Isaac Watts, 1719

questions.q: “Silver Bells” was written for which Bob Hope movie?
questions.reveal: The Lemon Drop Kid (1951)! Jay Livingston and Ray Evans wrote it. Holiday Inn and White Christmas were Bing’s territory.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Silver Bells — Jay Livingston & Ray Evans, 1950

questions.category: Do You Hear What I Hear?
questions.q: Its writers said “Do You Hear What I Hear?” (1962) was a plea for peace during what event?
questions.reveal: The Cuban Missile Crisis, October 1962. Married songwriters Noël Regney and Gloria Shayne wrote it as a prayer for peace. Heavy stuff for a song that starts with a lamb.

refs.label: Song
refs.ref: Do You Hear What I Hear? — Noël Regney & Gloria Shayne, 1962
